title: 18 dodecahedra in an octahedron

contribution.method:
Batch of 632 witnesses in 23 problems (`MANIFEST.json` + `records/<record_id>.json` + `SUMMARY.tsv`), each at least 1e-4 (relative) below the current `records/SUMMARY.csv` entry (main at e0fc3211, checked 2026-10-26). Every record passes `verify_general.py` (VALID) and `certify_general.py` (CERTIFIED) from that commit locally, run on the files extracted from the archive. The changes against the current records: median -8.63 %, largest -21.13 %; 563 records improve by ≥ 1 %, 630 by ≥ 0.1 %.

**Against the pending PolyPack submissions.** Issues #101 and #102 (sinkomr, still open) contain values for 484 of these records. I compared with PolyPack's published records (https://github.com/sinkomr/PolyPack, `data/polyhedra/records.json`, fetched 2026-10-26) and kept only records that are at least 1e-4 below both the current archive and PolyPack. If those two batches are accepted first, this batch stays valid; `SUMMARY.tsv` lists both values (`polypack_s`, `change_vs_best`).

**How the records were made.** None of these records starts from a catalogue configuration of the same problem, so all carry my own `found_by`; `method` gives the steps.

- *Lattice cuts* (550): all pieces in one orientation at the points of a lattice inside the container, orientation and position of the container optimised, then a contact-preserving descent. For 147 of them the lattice packing was made for a larger n and the record keeps its first n pieces (descended again); `derived_from` names that n. Rigidity analysis and code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23630728
- *Cell compositions* (82): the container is divided into cells (pyramids from the centre of an icosahedron, tetrahedral–octahedral honeycomb cells, cube grids) and each cell is filled with a catalogue record or with a single piece. `method` names the cells; the catalogue records placed in the cells and their finders are listed in `uses_records` (79 records).

Clearance: centres expanded by 3e-7 about the origin, container sized from th
